# One-Day Meal Plan for Strength Training and Muscle Gain

Here is a customized one-day meal plan for an 85 kg athlete focused on building muscle and optimizing post-workout recovery:

* **Calorie Target:** Approximately 3,200 calories
* **Macronutrient Breakdown:** Protein (180g), Fat (95g), Carbs (420g)

## Meal Plan:

* **Breakfast (7:00 AM):** Scrambled eggs (3 whole eggs, 150g), oatmeal (100g dry weight) with honey (20g), and whole milk (240g).
  * Protein: 28g | Fat: 18g | Carbs: 65g

* **Mid-Morning Snack (10:00 AM):** Greek yogurt (200g, full-fat) with granola (50g) and blueberries (80g).
  * Protein: 20g | Fat: 8g | Carbs: 55g

* **Pre-Workout Snack (12:30 PM):** Banana (150g) with peanut butter (30g) and white bread (40g).
  * Protein: 10g | Fat: 16g | Carbs: 60g

* **Lunch (2:00 PM):** Grilled chicken breast (180g), brown rice (150g cooked), and steamed asparagus (150g) with olive oil (15g).
  * Protein: 45g | Fat: 12g | Carbs: 65g

* **Post-Workout Snack (5:00 PM):** Chocolate milk (400g, whole milk) with whey protein powder (30g).
  * Protein: 35g | Fat: 8g | Carbs: 50g

* **Dinner (7:30 PM):** Lean ground beef (180g, 90/10), sweet potato (200g baked), and mixed green salad (150g) with olive oil dressing (20g).
  * Protein: 40g | Fat: 20g | Carbs: 65g

* **Evening Snack (9:30 PM):** Cottage cheese (150g, full-fat) with almonds (25g).
  * Protein: 27g | Fat: 13g | Carbs: 20g

---

**Plan Benefits:** This meal plan emphasizes high-quality protein sources distributed strategically across 7 meals, supports muscle protein synthesis, and features carbohydrate timing around your workout for optimal energy and recovery. Healthy fats support hormone production and overall performance. The calorie surplus and macronutrient ratios are designed specifically to support strength gains and muscle hypertrophy for your body composition and training goals.

# One-Day Meal Plan for Marathon Training

Here is a one-day meal plan for a vegetarian athlete optimizing endurance performance with carbohydrate-focused nutrition:

* **Calorie Target:** Approximately 3,000 calories
* **Macronutrient Breakdown:** Protein (105g), Fat (75g), Carbs (450g)

## Meal Plan:

* **Breakfast (7:00 AM):** Oatmeal (80g dry weight) with banana (120g), honey (25g), whole milk (240g), and sunflower seeds (20g).
* Protein: 16g, Fat: 12g, Carbs: 95g

* **Mid-Morning Snack (10:00 AM):** Greek yogurt (200g, full-fat) with granola (45g) and dried apricots (40g).
* Protein: 18g, Fat: 8g, Carbs: 68g

* **Pre-Run Snack (12:30 PM):** White bread (60g) with honey (20g) and jam (15g).
* Protein: 5g, Fat: 2g, Carbs: 78g

* **Lunch (2:00 PM):** Lentil and vegetable curry (250g cooked lentils and vegetables), basmati rice (180g cooked), and olive oil (10g).
* Protein: 22g, Fat: 10g, Carbs: 95g

* **Post-Run Snack (5:30 PM):** Chocolate milk (400g, whole milk) with whey protein powder (25g).
* Protein: 32g, Fat: 12g, Carbs: 65g

* **Dinner (7:30 PM):** Chickpea and spinach stir-fry (200g chickpeas, 150g spinach), jasmine rice (160g cooked), and sesame oil (10g).
* Protein: 16g, Fat: 15g, Carbs: 85g

* **Evening Snack (9:30 PM):** Whole grain bread (50g) with tahini (15g) and dates (30g).
* Protein: 6g, Fat: 8g, Carbs: 50g

---

**Nutritional Summary:** This plan prioritizes complex carbohydrates strategically timed around training to maximize glycogen stores and endurance performance. The 450g carbs represent 60% of total calories, ideal for marathon training. Protein (105g) supports muscle recovery and repair, while healthy fats from seeds, oils, and tahini support hormone production and nutrient absorption. All meals exclude nuts (sesame seeds and tahini substitute for nut butters) and use vegetarian protein sources including legumes, dairy, and plant-based options. The timing supports a morning running session with pre- and post-run nutrition for optimal recovery.
